findings.text: Init constructor for AMD support checks boot CPU vendor and family and on success hands back the AMD operation table, otherwise reports unsupported and returns no table.
Module exit path releases all AMD loader state by discarding the equivalence table and the patch cache.
Early boot loader scans initrd containers for AMD microcode, ignores non-AMD or old families and disabled loader, and preloads the selected container into the internal cache.
Firmware request handler chooses a generic or family specific binary name, fetches it directly, validates the container, loads patches into cache, then releases the firmware.

Load pipeline progresses from container parse to cache fill to per-node freshness check, yielding not-found when suppressed, error on validation or allocation failure, ok when loaded but current, and new when any node trails its cached patch.

Equivalence table install always validates the header and advances past it, but only pre-Zen families allocate and copy the table and derive entry count from its length; Zen and newer skip storage yet still report consumed size, and free is a no-op there.

Single patch ingest validates the section and its claimed size, allocates a patch descriptor plus a private copy of the payload, records processor and patch identifiers from the embedded header, initializes its list linkage, and inserts it into the cache.
Loader disable is sticky: once set it stays set, and it becomes set when running under a hypervisor without debug build or when current AMD patch level matches the final list.
Final-level check applies only to AMD CPUs, reads the current patch level from hardware, and scans a zero-terminated list for an exact match.
Vendor detection issues CPUID leaf zero and compares the three identifier registers against known Intel and AMD triples, defaulting to unknown.
AMD operation table provides callbacks for firmware request, CPU info collection, application, per-CPU teardown and late-load finalization, and flags the path as NMI safe.
Known-hash table is a static array where each entry pairs a numeric patch identifier with a 32-byte digest.
Minimum AMD family for loader is hex 10, family hex 15 selects family-specific firmware file naming, family hex 17 is the threshold where equivalence table storage is skipped.
Log lines carry a microcode prefix, and firmware lives under amd-ucode with a generic binary name or a family-specific variant for newer families.
Any verification or allocation failure during container load aborts with error status and discards partial state, and failed late load also triggers full cleanup to prevent use of incomplete cache.

Per-CPU teardown clears the cached microcode reference for the target CPU; global loader state lives in an ops pointer, a sticky disable flag, base and per-CPU revision values, and a hypervisor-present flag.
